layers.item: Tax on the act of converting or remitting
layers.blank_reason: No conversion or remittance tax appears in the foreign-exchange rules read; that is an absence in the sources, not an official statement of nil.
layers.when: The rules ask for a real, lawful basis and documents. Current-account payments are not restricted.

layers.item: Chinese income tax on the money itself, if it was never paid
layers.amount: 3%–45% on salary-type income; 5%–35% on business income; 20% flat on interest, dividends, rental, asset-transfer and incidental income
layers.when: The bank sells foreign exchange against proof of source that includes tax vouchers, so unpaid tax has to be settled first. Your own figure depends on facts not provided.

layers.item: Tax paperwork for a single payment above USD 50,000
layers.amount: No charge stated; a filing with the tax bureau
layers.when: A foreign individual's China pay, dividends, interest and similar items sent abroad in one payment above USD 50,000. One filing covers repeat payments under the same contract.

layers.item: Bank's conversion margin (Bank of China board)
layers.amount: {{margin_pct}} of the amount, one way against the board midpoint
layers.when: Every purchase of USD at the bank. Computed from the 17:39:58 board: (668.51 − 667.11) ÷ 667.11.

layers.amount: 0.1% of the amount, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260, plus CNY 150 cable fee per wire
layers.when: Every outward telegraphic transfer; same price online and at the counter.

layers.amount: USD 25 per wire with the full-amount option (USD 15 if the receiving bank has an account at BOC New York)
layers.when: Without the option, intermediary deductions are passed on at cost and are not published.

layers.amount: USD 15 at Chase and Bank of America; none at Schwab
layers.when: Per incoming wire. Which institution you use was not provided.

layers.blank_reason: No US tax on an incoming transfer of your own money was found in the sources read. The 1% remittance tax applies where the sender hands cash, a money order or a cashier's check to a remittance provider.
layers.when: Listed so the 1% remittance tax is not mistaken for a tax on money arriving from China.

layers.item: US income tax on the money itself
layers.blank_reason: Depends on what the income was and whether it was reported when earned; not provided.
layers.when: A US citizen's worldwide income is generally taxable wherever earned. Chinese income tax paid on the same income can generally be credited.

layers.item: Currency gain when the yuan is turned into dollars
layers.amount: Per USD 10,000 converted today: gain of {{gain_2024_10k}} if the yuan was acquired at the 2024 average rate, {{gain_2025_10k}} at the 2025 rate, {{gain_2023_10k}} at the 2023 rate, {{gain_2022_10k}} at the 2022 rate; a loss of {{loss_2021_10k}} at the 2021 rate
layers.when: Disposing of foreign currency, including a foreign-currency bank deposit, is a section 988 transaction. For a personal transaction no gain is recognised unless the gain on the transaction exceeds USD 200. The tax itself is the gain times your own rate, which was not provided.

layers.item: Reporting duties (no tax, but penalties if missed)
layers.amount: FBAR when foreign accounts together exceed USD 10,000 at any time in the year; Form 8938 from USD 50,000 at year-end or USD 75,000 at any time (single filer living in the US); Form 3520 for foreign gifts or bequests above USD 100,000 in a year
layers.when: The Chinese account itself is reportable while it holds the money. Higher Form 8938 thresholds apply to joint filers and to people living abroad.

penalties.trigger: Moving foreign exchange abroad in breach of the rules, or moving capital abroad by deception (逃汇)
penalties.penalty: Order to bring the money back; fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% in serious cases; criminal liability possible

penalties.trigger: Buying foreign exchange with false or invalid documents (非法套汇)
penalties.penalty: Conversion reversed; fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% in serious cases; criminal liability possible

penalties.trigger: Private or disguised foreign-exchange trading, including through underground banks
penalties.penalty: Warning; confiscation of gains; fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% in serious cases; criminal liability possible

penalties.trigger: Published case: 19 underground-bank trades totalling USD 3.331 million (2021)
penalties.penalty: Fine CNY 2.157 million; recorded in the central bank's credit system

penalties.trigger: Published case: 48 underground-bank trades totalling USD 3.077 million (2022–2023)
penalties.penalty: Fine CNY 1.672 million; recorded in the central bank's credit system

penalties.trigger: Splitting, or borrowing or lending the USD 50,000 quota
penalties.penalty: Watch list for the listing year and the next 2 years; every exchange then needs documents

penalties.trigger: Submitting untrue documents, or failing to make the balance-of-payments declaration
penalties.penalty: Warning; fine up to CNY 50,000 for an individual

penalties.trigger: Carrying foreign exchange across the border in breach of the rules
penalties.penalty: Warning; fine up to 20% of the amount

penalties.trigger: Undeclared cash above the customs limit, not concealed
penalties.penalty: Warning; fine up to 20% of the excess; excess sent back

penalties.trigger: Overseas ATM cash above CNY 100,000 in a calendar year
penalties.penalty: Overseas cash withdrawals suspended for that year and the next
Up to USD 16,536 per report (figure for penalties assessed on or after 17 Jan 2025)
Up to the greater of USD 165,353 or 50% of the account balance; can apply per account; criminal penalties possible
Up to USD 10,000, plus USD 10,000 for each 30 days after an IRS notice, to a maximum of USD 60,000; criminal penalties possible

penalties.trigger: Form 3520 late, incomplete or incorrect (foreign gift or bequest above USD 100,000)
penalties.blank_reason: The IRS page read points to penalties under section 6039F(c) without stating the rate.

penalties.trigger: Carrying more than USD 10,000 in cash into the US without filing FinCEN Form 105
penalties.penalty: Seizure of the cash; civil or criminal penalties possible

relief.route: Late FBARs, income already reported and tax paid
relief.terms: File the late FBARs online with a statement of why they are late. The IRS will not impose a penalty if the foreign income was properly reported and taxed and it has not already contacted you about those years.

relief.route: Streamlined procedures, living in the United States
relief.terms: Certify the failure was not willful, file the returns, and pay a single penalty of 5% of the foreign financial assets involved. Example on the IRS page: USD 130,000 × 5% = USD 6,500.

relief.route: Streamlined procedures, living outside the United States
relief.terms: Certify the failure was not willful and file the returns; all penalties are waived for eligible taxpayers.
The streamlined procedures are not available; the IRS points to its Criminal Investigation Voluntary Disclosure Practice.
The streamlined procedures cannot be used after the IRS has started a civil examination or a criminal investigation.
